ceiling_directive: Prove an output-sensitive quotient-enumeration algorithm on the removed-set DAG that emits each distinct coefficient tuple once, with complexity polynomial in the 2^p state representation plus output size rather than the number of compatible orders.
improvement_directive: Complete the deferred duplicate-free tuple enumeration: quotient the removed-set DAG by equality of induced coefficient tuples and prove polynomial-delay or total output-sensitive bounds, then use it to compute the essential poset and minimum-calibration certificates without factorial path traversal.
critique: The note proves a complete arbitrary-observation-graph compatibility characterization, generic one-pair identification, and covariance-region recovery only for its own restrictive component-aligned Gaussian subclass, not for the published LiMVAM class motivating the project. The removed-set recursion constructs at most 2^p states, but extracting the distinct coefficient tuples can still require traversing factorially many compatible source-to-sink paths and deduplicating afterward, so the advertised output-size algorithm is not delivered. The minimum-calibration result likewise supplies an exact exhaustive search characterization rather than the stronger quotient-based computational procedure requested by the headline project. The framing is accurate about these limitations and does not falsely claim duplicate-free enumeration or a completed Cam-CAN application, but the proved contribution remains a specialized identification-and-inference framework rather than a field-level resolution of the broader LiMVAM calibration problem.
